question: Should OpenClaw expose a core filesystem path-policy config, and should the first supported contract cover exec or explicitly split exec to a separate policy?
rationale: This defines a public config API and a security enforcement boundary; current related PRs demonstrate competing shapes and unresolved exec coverage.

options.title: Settle one `tools.fs` contract
options.body: Choose a canonical allow/deny or roots model with deny precedence, normalization/symlink behavior, explicit exec scope, docs, and upgrade tests before landing implementation.

options.title: Land file-tool policy, split exec
options.body: Accept a file-tool/media/apply_patch first version only if shell-mediated access is clearly documented as out of scope and tracked by a linked exec policy item.

options.title: Defer to OS/container isolation
options.body: Decline host path ACL config for now and rely on OS users, Docker/SSH sandboxing, tool profiles, and `workspaceOnly` only.

recommendation.title: Settle one `tools.fs` contract
recommendation.body: Choose a canonical allow/deny or roots model with deny precedence, normalization/symlink behavior, explicit exec scope, docs, and upgrade tests before landing implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history and prior-review signal on the existing workspace-only filesystem boundary.
